title: Bank OTP disguised as delivery code vs. genuine delivery OTP
summary: A SwiftShip Couriers delivery agent calls about a ShopKart parcel and asks the recipient for a code. In the legitimate case, the agent is at the door and asks for the delivery OTP that ShopKart sent to confirm handover. In the fraud case, the caller has no parcel with them; the "code" they ask for arrives in a message from the recipient's bank or payment app and authorises a payment or account change. This family is a deliberate keyword confound: both callers ask for an OTP.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer who is expecting a delivery; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers give an agent name and mention the order.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks for a code that the recipient's message identifies as coming from their bank or payment app. Sharing it would authorise a transaction or account change, not a delivery.
stable_facts: The caller says the parcel is "on hold at the hub" and they need a code to "release" it for delivery.

The message that arrives is from Kaveri Bank or PaySetu, not from ShopKart. It mentions an amount [AMOUNT_6] (₹2,000–₹15,000). The recipient reads its sender or content aloud, or says it mentions an amount.
The caller is not at the door.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist the bank code is the release code or add urgency ("parcel will be returned"). They must not switch to asking for a link or a fee. The legitimate agent must not mention any payment or second code.

must_preserve: sender of the message (bank/app vs. ShopKart) stated by the recipient
must_not_emit: narrator explanations of what the code is

ambiguities: The word "OTP" and a request to share it appear in both cases. The label depends on what the code is, which must be made visible by the recipient's turn.
If generation fails to include F-E1, the prefix must be rejected, not relabelled.
A real delivery agent who happens to call while not yet at the door is plausible. In this family the legitimate agent is always present, so presence is a supporting cue, not a label rule.

evidence_references.claim: A major Indian marketplace uses a delivery OTP shared with the delivery executive at handover (C15)
Bank OTPs must not be shared with anyone (C01)
